column3: The Hebrew uses “spoke ... saying”; BSB condenses this to “said”.
The Hebrew repeats “speak ... saying” and expresses Moses’ mediation as “by the hand of Moses”; BSB condenses the speech formula and says “through Moses”.
The Hebrew joins “unintentionally” and “without knowledge” without an alternative “or”, and calls the person struck a “soul”.
The Hebrew says he shall speak “his words in the ears of the elders”; BSB states this as presenting his case before them.
Prior hatred is expressed literally as “from yesterday and the third day”; BSB summarizes it as “prior malice”.
The Hebrew separately repeats “his city”, “his house”, and “the city from which he fled”; BSB condenses this to his own home in that city.
The Hebrew has a singular “sojourner who sojourns” and calls the person killed a “soul”. BSB uses plural “foreigners” and supplies “trial” for the final standing before the assembly.
